title: Periodic table structure and blocks; Balanced equations and reacting masses; Molar gas volume and Avogadro's law; Empirical and molecular formulae
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for OCR A-level (A) Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: PT01#t1 term and clue written for the game; PT01#t3 term and clue written for the game; AM07#t4 term and clue written for the game; AM07#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: AM02#N.3, AM05#N.2, AM07#N.4a, PT01#N.6, AM02#N.5, AM05#N.4, AM07#N.6a, PT01#N.10, AM02#N.7a, AM05#N.7a, AM07#N.12a, PT01#N.12a.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Period
items.clue: A row of the table; its number gives the outer occupied shell.

items.label: Valence electrons
items.clue: The outer-shell particles of an atom: seven for bromine, 4s² 4p⁵.

items.label: Precipitate
items.clue: A solid formed when two solutions react, e.g. AgCl from Ag⁺ and Cl⁻.

items.label: State symbols
items.clue: The labels (s), (l), (g) and (aq) written after each species in an equation.

questions.stem: A compound contains 40.0% carbon, 6.7% hydrogen and 53.3% oxygen by mass. Its Mr is 60.0. What is its empirical formula?
questions.explanation: In 100 g: 3.33 mol C, about 6.6–6.7 mol H, 3.33 mol O. ÷ smallest: 1 : 2 : 1.

questions.stem: Two identical sealed flasks are at the same temperature and pressure. One is filled with methane, CH₄, and the other with chlorine, Cl₂. The methane flask contains 5.00 × 10²² atoms in total. How many atoms does the chlorine flask contain? (Ar: H 1.0, C 12.0, Cl 35.5)
questions.explanation: Equal molecules: 5.00 × 10²² ÷ 5 = 1.00 × 10²² CH₄ molecules, so 1.00 × 10²² Cl₂ molecules = 2.00 × 10²² atoms.

questions.stem: Aluminium burns in oxygen to form aluminium oxide. Which equation for this reaction is correctly balanced?
questions.explanation: Al₂O₃ and O₂ are the right formulae. 3O₂ gives 6 O = 2Al₂O₃, which needs 4Al. 4 Al and 6 O each side.

questions.stem: Germanium is in period 4, group 14. Which is the full electron configuration of a germanium atom?
questions.explanation: Period 4, p-block: fill up to 4p. Group 14 gives 14 − 10 = 4 valence electrons, 4s² 4p². With the 3d¹⁰, the total is 32 electrons.

questions.stem: A compound of aluminium and sulfur contains 35.93% aluminium and 64.07% sulfur by mass. What is its empirical formula? Data: Ar Al 27.0, S 32.1.
questions.explanation: Divide each mass by its atomic mass: Al 1.33, S 2.00. Ratio 1 : 1.50; × 2 = 2 : 3.

questions.stem: Sulfur dioxide reacts with oxygen: 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2SO₃(g). What volume of oxygen reacts completely with 30.0 cm³ of sulfur dioxide? All volumes are measured at the same temperature and pressure.
questions.explanation: Same T and p, so volumes are in the coefficient ratio: 30.0 × 1/2 = 15.0 cm³.

questions.stem: Magnesium ribbon fizzes and dissolves in dilute hydrochloric acid. Which is the ionic equation for the reaction?
questions.explanation: Cl⁻ is a spectator. 1 Mg and 2 H each side; charge 2+ each side.

questions.stem: An element has the ground-state electron configuration 1s²2s²2p⁶3s²3p⁴. What is the typical charge of the ions of this element in its ionic compounds?
questions.explanation: The atom has six valence electrons, 3s²3p⁴. It gains two electrons, giving a valence shell of eight and two more electrons than protons: a charge of −2, as in sulfide.

questions.stem: A hydrocarbon contains 88.80% carbon and 11.20% hydrogen by mass. Its Mr is 54.0. What is its molecular formula? (Ar: H 1.0, C 12.0)

Magnesium reacts with excess dilute hydrochloric acid: Mg(s) + 2HCl(aq) → MgCl₂(aq) + H₂(g). What volume of hydrogen, in cm³ at RTP, forms from 0.120 g of magnesium? (Ar: Mg 24.3; molar gas volume 24.0 dm³ mol⁻¹ at RTP)

Iron is produced by reducing iron(III) oxide with carbon monoxide: Fe₂O₃(s) + 3CO(g) → 2Fe(s) + 3CO₂(g). What is the maximum mass of iron that can be produced from 40.0 g of iron(III) oxide? (Ar: O 16.0, Fe 55.8)
Beryllium, 1s² 2s², and helium, 1s², both have two electrons in their outer s sub-shell. Why is beryllium placed in group 2, but helium in group 18?

options.text: Beryllium is a solid and helium is a gas, and group 18 holds the gaseous elements.
Beryllium has four electrons and helium two, and the group number counts the total.
Beryllium's 2s² electrons are in a higher shell, so they are inner electrons, not valence electrons.
Beryllium's outer shell, n = 2, is far from full, while helium's n = 1 shell is full with just two.
